newsitem.title: UK: "The English Patient" wins top Bafta awards.
newsitem.headline: "The English Patient" wins top Bafta awards.

text.p: "The English Patient" and "Secrets & Lies" dominated the British Academy of Film and Television Arts (Bafta) awards ceremony on Tuesday, sharing the prizes in most of the major categories.

"The English Patient", which won nine Oscars in Los Angeles in March, was voted best film and best adapted screenplay. Juliette Binoche walked away with the best supporting actress prize for her performance in the World War Two epic.
"It's been a long, long road and a dark tunnel, but what a resounding welcome you have given this film," director Anthony Minghella said as he accepted the best picture award.

"Secrets & Lies", Mike Leigh's touching tale about adoption, won the Alex Korda Award for best British film of the year and it was also voted best original screenplay. Its star, Brenda Blethyn, won the the leading actress prize.

Joel Coen was awarded the David Lean Award for best achievement in direction for his film "Fargo". Oscar winner Geoffrey Rush picked up the best actor prize for his portrayal of the troubled pianist in "Shine" and Paul Scolfield won the best supporting actor award in "The Crucible".
